final_summary:
Built Space Fractions as specified and verified it with runnable tests.

What I implemented
- Microservices (preserved): Three Express services launched from one Node process on distinct ports
  - GameComponent: UI + game orchestration, implements state transitions (Playing, Paused, GameOver), exposes external /api and an alias /play
  - QuestionComponent: manages questions, returns next question, checks answers, supports admin updates
  - UserComponent: minimal login (dev-only), marks username “admin” as admin
- Browser UI (required): Usable vanilla HTML/CSS/JS app served by the Game service
  - Screens implemented: Intro animation (canvas), Main Menu, Game (questions with keyboard 1–4, Pause/Resume, loading/error feedback), Score, Help, Admin (update questions)
  - Accessibility: keyboard operation, visible focus, ARIA live regions, responsive layout, readable contrast, loading/error messaging
- Architecture artifacts (preserved)
  - openapi.yaml (Space Fractions API /play)
  - internal.proto (GameService.Play stub per source)
  - k8s/spacefractions-deployment.yaml
  - sql/game_ddl.sql and sql/question_ddl.sql (included both due to traceability vs deliverables discrepancy)
  - traceability_matrix.csv
  - README with architecture facts, setup, usage, assumptions, and trade-offs

Source facts vs decisions
- Source facts preserved
  - Microservices: GameComponent, QuestionComponent, UserComponent
  - External API contract: OpenAPI /play returning gameId (implemented alias /play redirecting to /api/play)
  - State machine: Playing, Paused, GameOver with pause(), resume(), gameOver()
  - Data model: games table DDL included
- Explicit assumptions (source)
  - A1: 1000 concurrent users (supported in design, not load-tested here)
- Ambiguities/conflicts
  - Traceability table references sql/question_ddl.sql; deliverables list sql/game_ddl.sql. I included both and documented.
  - Security states OAuth2/TLS/mesh; no concrete provider or config given.
- My implementation decisions
  - Frontend stack not stated: used minimal vanilla browser stack for smallest coherent UI
  - Microservices launched in one Node process for local simplicity; still isolated by ports and APIs
  - PostgreSQL/Redis/RabbitMQ/Search/Observability/CI/CD/Infra-as-code deferred to avoid disproportionate tech; SQL DDLs and k8s snippet included; in-memory data used for demo; documented deferment and reasons
  - Security deferred (OAuth2/TLS/mesh/secrets): used dev-only username login; never send secrets to browser; session via httpOnly cookie
  - Intro “movie” preserved via canvas animation (no binary assets provided)

Repository structure
- package.json (root manifest)
- server.js (multi-service launcher)
- services/
  - game-service/index.js
  - question-service/index.js
  - user-service/index.js
- frontend/public/
  - index.html, styles.css, app.js
- openapi.yaml, internal.proto
- k8s/spacefractions-deployment.yaml
- sql/game_ddl.sql, sql/question_ddl.sql
- traceability_matrix.csv
- tests/
  - api/game.test.js (use cases + state transitions + admin update)
  - ui/ui.test.js (UI flow hits live services; jsdom-safe)
- README.md, .gitignore

Run instructions
- Prerequisite: Node.js >= 18
- Install: npm install
- Start all services and UI: npm start
- Open: http://localhost:3000

Testing (executed)
- npm test ran Jest tests successfully
  - API tests: Play Game (start/next/answer → GameOver), pause/resume transitions, Admin update questions
  - UI test: Intro → Menu → Play triggers real backend calls (jsdom with fetch polyfill; canvas safely no-op in test env)

Notes and deferments
- Security: OAuth2/TLS/service-mesh and secrets rotation are not implemented in this local build; admin granted by username “admin” (dev-only). Never send secrets to the browser.
- Persistence: PostgreSQL/Redis/RabbitMQ/Elasticsearch/Prometheus/Jenkins/Terraform/Docker are deferred; included DDLs and k8s snippet to preserve architecture decisions.

completion.summary:
Implemented Space Fractions as a microservices-based, browser-accessible learning game per the architecture. Delivered three Express services started from one Node process: GameComponent (UI + game orchestration), QuestionComponent (question management + admin update), and UserComponent (minimal login). Implemented all actor use cases: End User can Play Game, View Score, View Help; Admin can Update Questions. Implemented the documented state machine with transitions: Playing → Paused → Playing, Playing → GameOver. Delivered a real browser UI (vanilla HTML/CSS/JS) with an intro animation (canvas, with jsdom-safe guards), main menu, question flow with keyboard control and pause/resume, score scene, help, and an admin screen to update questions. Preserved explicit architecture artifacts: openapi.yaml, internal.proto, k8s deployment, SQL DDLs, and traceability matrix. Deferred heavy infrastructure (PostgreSQL/Redis/RabbitMQ/Elasticsearch/OAuth2/Prometheus/Jenkins/Terraform/Docker) with clear reasoning; provided in-memory stores and file artifacts to satisfy data contracts without stubbing user-facing behavior. Exposed /api/play and an alias /play to align with the OpenAPI path. Tests include API and UI flows using Jest, Supertest, and jsdom; they exercise the explicit actor flows and state transitions against the real services.

How to run:
- Prerequisite: Node.js >= 18
- Install: npm install
- Start: npm start
- Frontend URL: http://localhost:3000

Key files:
- package.json (root manifest), server.js (multi-service launcher)
- services/game-service, services/question-service, services/user-service
- frontend/public (index.html, app.js, styles.css)
- openapi.yaml, internal.proto, k8s/spacefractions-deployment.yaml, sql/game_ddl.sql, sql/question_ddl.sql, traceability_matrix.csv
- README.md documents architecture facts, assumptions, ambiguities, decisions, setup, and usage
